objectives: Provide targeted practice for weak /w/ components identified by the diagnostic.
Reassess each remediated component with fresh items.
Route learners to advancement or further targeted reteaching.
concepts: Remediation should match the diagnosed weakness.
Fresh items test transfer rather than memorization.

definitions.definition: Focused teaching and practice addressing a specific identified weakness.
A fresh assessment used after remediation to determine whether the skill has become secure.
Applying a learned skill successfully to new items or contexts.

workedExamples: If initial /w/ recognition is weak, practise hearing and mapping /w/ before reassessment.
If encoding is weak, segment fresh w-CVC words, write them, read them back, then reassess.
If comprehension is weak, practise locating text evidence before answering fresh questions.
commonMistakes: Remediating every skill when only one is weak.
Using the exact diagnostic items again.
Confusing accurate decoding with complete comprehension.
keyTakeaways: Advance only when mastery evidence supports it.

basic: Practise the specific weak /w/ component identified by the diagnostic.
conceptual: Match a diagnostic error to an appropriate remediation activity.
application: Complete fresh w-CVC reassessment items after remediation.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why fresh items provide stronger evidence of mastery.
mixedReview: Integrate sound, decoding, encoding, comprehension and fluency remediation.

formulaOrFactBank: mastery = 80% or higher on the relevant reassessment
mistakeBasedRevision: If mastery is not reached, return to the specific weak component rather than restarting the whole cycle.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat only the component-specific practice indicated by the latest evidence.

outcomes: Learner receives targeted practice matched to diagnosed weakness.
Learner demonstrates the remediated skill on fresh items.
System advances learners at or above 80% and routes others for further reteaching.
